source.title: Improved guarantees and a multiple-descent curve for the Column Subset Selection Problem and the Nyström method
source.authors: Michal Derezinski; Rekha Khanna; Michael W. Mahoney

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses double descent but studies CSSP/Nyström approximation factors, not test or generalization error of learning models. Its results therefore do not test any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper explicitly compares its multiple-descent phenomenon with double descent, while distinguishing its deterministic subset-selection task and approximation-factor measure from generalization error. The paper's own CSSP/Nyström results are recorded under fits_no_version. Results it cites from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The paper studies the approximation factor of column subset selection and Nyström kernel approximation as subset size k varies. It draws parallels to double descent but measures no test error, risk or generalization error of a learning model. Its curves track a different construct, so no version is tested. It also does not use double descent as a tool (not T4). Its multiple-descent findings belong under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors derive spectrum-dependent upper bounds and a lower-bound construction, showing the CSSP/Nyström approximation factor can have multiple peaks and valleys in k. They argue this is inherent to the task, not an artifact of the analysis, and demonstrate it on real data by varying the RBF σ. They call it a possible connection to double descent but stress that their setting is deterministic and uses relative approximation error, not generalization error.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes column subset selection and Nyström kernel approximation using k-DPP and greedy selection, measuring approximation factors against subset size. It does not train deep networks or measure test error.
record.method_sensitivity: The approximation-factor curves change with the spectrum and, in the RBF experiments, with σ; the toy experiments vary condition number κ. The greedy curve is described as algorithm-dependent, and not every spectral drop produces a peak.

fits_no_version.finding: Theory (Theorem 3, Corollary 1) constructs matrices whose optimal CSSP approximation factor alternates between ≤1+δ and ≥(1−δ)(k+1) across a sequence of subset sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The optimal CSSP/Nyström approximation factor can show multiple peaks and valleys in subset size k, with peaks at sharp spectral drops.

fits_no_version.finding: Under k-DPP Nyström selection, peaks in the approximation factor align with spectral drops. Larger drops (higher κ or σ) give sharper or multiple peaks. Flat spectra (small σ) eliminate the peaks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Nyström approximation-factor multiple descent appears with sharp spectral drops and vanishes under smooth spectral decay.

fits_no_version.finding: Greedy selection shows similar peaks. However, not every spectral drop produces a peak, and the curve's shape is algorithm-dependent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Greedy Nyström approximation factors show multiple descent aligned with some, but not all, spectral drops.

record.problems: The reported empirical curves are presented in figures, with numerical curve values not stated in the text. The k-DPP experiment reports three times the standard error of the mean over 1000 trials; the greedy experiment reports no uncertainty information. The results concern approximation factors, not model generalization or test error.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant results were left out.

untested.parts: All: no deep networks and no test error versus model size.
All: no sample-count effect on test error.
All: the measure is the approximation factor of a deterministic subset-selection task, not risk past an interpolation point.
All: stable rank bounds the approximation factor, not test-error peak locations.
All: the multiple peaks concern the approximation factor, not risk. There is no label noise or regularization tuning.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 1 has a k-DPP experiment on a matrix with two spectral drops, compared against the bounds. It has no row, but it bears only on fits_no_version, not on any version. The double-descent parallels the paper cites (Poggio, Liao, Liang, Bartlett) are other works' results and should not be rows. The record's T6/discusses classification is correct.

versions.untested_parts: Model-wise test error in deep networks, model size, and the interpolation threshold.
The effect of training-sample count on test error near interpolation.
Risk across model classes as capacity grows past an interpolation point; CSSP/Nyström approximation factors are a different measure and task.
Whether a single effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.
Noise, variance, triple or multiple descent in model risk, and optimally tuned regularization.
Whether re-counting model complexity as effective parameters turns a second descent into a U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: matrix A constructed for Theorem 3
rows.size_stated: m × n; dimensions otherwise not stated
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 3 constructs a matrix with lower bounds on the CSSP approximation factor at a sequence of subset sizes.
rows.measure: CSSP projection error divided by OPT_ki
rows.value: For every subset S of size ki, the ratio is at least (1 − δ)(ki − ki−1), for i = 1,...,t.
rows.note: This is a theoretical CSSP approximation-factor result, not a model test-error result.

rows.subject: matrix A whose optimal CSSP subsets exhibit multiple peaks and valleys
rows.operation_detail: Corollary 1 gives upper and lower bounds on the optimal CSSP approximation factor at alternating subset sizes.
rows.measure: Minimum CSSP projection error divided by OPT at each specified subset size
rows.value: At kil the minimum ratio is ≤ 1 + δ; at kiu it is ≥ (1 − δ)(kiu + 1), for each i.
rows.note: The authors call this a multiple-descent curve for CSSP; it is not test or generalization error.
